messages:
rebecca_h: Heads-up — Veridian reported weird embedding drift after we merged their LoRA adapter into the int4-quant mainline. Quick summary: local smoke pack passed, but customer eval shows top-1 intent mismatch ~12% vs baseline 2%. Suspect tokenization/embedding shift. Anyone seen this pattern?

sanjay: Noted. Do we have the exact adapter+base combos and quant profile?

rebecca_h: Adapter: veridian_lora_v3.bin, base: redwood-7b-int4-q4f16 (tag: release-2026-03-15), tokenizer: transformer-tokenizer v2.1. Config: 
```
merge_strategy: additive
alpha: 0.8
quant_profile: q4f16-fast
```
Local quick-eval (on our 200-sample smoke set): top1_accuracy delta = -0.7% (within noise). Customer evaluation (1k samples) shows -12% on certain invoice parsing prompts.

omar: Could be prefix caching or token alignment when merging adapters. Did they re-run with our canonical tokenizer?

rebecca_h: They said they used shipped tokenizer but may have older vocab. Verifying now.

lucy: Also check embedding drift specifically for numeric spans — we saw previous adapter merges that subtly shifted numeric token boundaries, hurting exact-match parsers. Cheap check: compare tokenization of a failing example across vocab versions.

rebecca_h: Running token diff now. Example: "Invoice # 00234-AB"
- tokenized (veridian customer tokenizer): ["Invoice","#","002","34","-","AB"]
- tokenized (canonical v2.1): ["Invoice","#","00234","-","AB"]

rebecca_h: So they split the numeric chunk differently. That explains downstream embed mismatch for numeric-aware prompts.

omar: Bingo. Two follow-ups: 1) Is the adapter sensitive to tokenization changes (i.e., LoRA learned embeddings aligned to token boundaries)? 2) Mitigation path: either remap tokens at serving time or recommend retraining the adapter with canonical tokenizer.

eval-bot: quick-eval results for veridian_lora_v3 on subset 100 samples:
- base(redwood-7b-int4-q4f16) top1: 81.2%
- base+adapter (customer tokenizer) top1: 69.5%
- base+adapter (canonical tokenizer) top1: 80.4%
(note: eval uses default batching, deterministic seed)

sanjay: That delta between customer tokenizer and canonical is telling. We should prepare a remediation checklist for the CS/SE team: 
1) confirm tokenizer vocab version on their infra
2) try token remapping shim at request time (quick workaround)
3) if no luck, propose small LoRA re-fit on canonical tokenizer (cheap 1-2 epochs)

rebecca_h: I'll draft the checklist and a tiny remapping snippet for SEs. Draft snippet: 
```
# pseudo remap: collapse numeric tokens
def collapse_numeric_tokens(tokens):
    out=[]
    buf=""
    for t in tokens:
        if t.isdigit() or (t.replace('-', '').isdigit()):
            buf += t
        else:
            if buf: out.append(buf); buf=""
            out.append(t)
    if buf: out.append(buf)
    return out
```
This is hacky but may recover many invoice cases.

lucy: Also add a regression test to our quickpack: include 50 invoice-like templates, tokenized with both tokenizers, run embeddings similarity (cosine) and intent accuracy. If adapter consistently drops on customer tokenizer, block merge for that adapter until remap or retrain.

omar: Agree. I'll add an automated check in the merge CI: if >10% top1 drop between canonical vs customer tokenizers on quickpack -> fail and flag for SE.

rebecca_h: Perfect. I'll ping SE and customer with diagnostics and the remap snippet now. Thanks all. :raised_hands:

eval-bot: Log uploaded: https://internal.redwood.dev/evals/6181239876/veridian-quickpack-logs (access: eng-ml, cust-se)
